comments.body: Sequencing note (2026-09-07): the held-out merge epic (traitorous-official-sunbittern) later merges 88 twin modules and renames 78 more, which changes about 170 modules' node ids and invalidates the `.test_durations` keys this story records. Rule: this story records the profile once as specified; the merge epic's last story awake-shoddy-gyrfalcon re-runs the same `--store-durations --clean-durations` command as its final step and commits the refreshed file (a note is posted there).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`pytest-split==0.11.0` is pinned (`pyproject.toml:274`) but `.test_durations` is git-ignored as "never committed" (`.gitignore:64-65`, task 9ad9), so no duration profile exists for splitting the suite or for the AGENTS.md 20-25 minute `make verify` budget. This story runs last in the epic so the profile covers the final suite after S1-S4. Line numbers re-checked on origin/main 6080140e7af (2026-10-26); the earlier cites were from an old commit.

## Approach
1. Remove the `.test_durations` entry and its comment (`.gitignore:64-65`).
2. Add `\.test_durations` to the `check-added-large-files` `exclude` (`.pre-commit-config.yaml:33`, now `^uv\.lock$`), making it `^(uv\.lock|\.test_durations)$`, and extend the comment above it (the 500 KB default cap would reject the file).
3. Record the profile in the SAME run as the pre-push gate. `make test` runs `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n $(PYTEST_WORKERS) --dist worksteal -q` (`Makefile:568`; `PYTEST_WORKERS ?= 4`, Makefile:72, the default used here), so `PYTEST_ADDOPTS="--store-durations --clean-durations --durations-path=$PWD/.rebar/scratch/test_durations.json" make verify` writes the profile and gives the `make verify` result in one pass instead of two full suites; `cp` then installs it as `.test_durations`. The default path cannot be used: the first attempt (2026-10-26 00:11 PDT) wrote `.test_durations` into the checkout and the repo-isolation backstop (`tests/_isolation.py:150`) failed the session with `?? .test_durations`; once tracked, a refresh would show as modified and fail the same way. `.rebar/*` is git-ignored. A clean `make lint typecheck import-convention` is a precondition, since `make verify` stops at the first failing prerequisite before `test`. pytest-split writes on the controller's `pytest_sessionfinish` (`pytest_split/plugin.py:188-223`), keyed by node id for every report with a non-negative duration, so xdist workers, skipped tests and the 17 known pandoc failures are included.
4. Commit `.test_durations` (sorted JSON, indent 4; size recorded on the ticket).
5. Add `### Per-test durations (.test_durations)` to `docs/local-dev-env.md` after the "Sandboxed agent hosts" section and before `### The per-test hang budget`: the command above and why it writes to `.rebar/` and copies, that the file is refreshed by a deliberate re-run only, that durations are one loaded run's wall-clock times (relative weights, not a budget), that groups are balanced by duration so counts differ (no hard numbers, they go stale at each refresh), and `pytest --splits N --group K` usage.
6. Exempt the profile from three repo-wide scans of tracked text, each flagging test node ids that quote retired names or fake secrets. Found one by one: (a) the criteria-vocabulary gate flagged 19 lines (`pre-commit run --all-files`, lint hook): add `Path(".test_durations")` to `EXCLUDED_FILES` in `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` (precedent: `scripts/build_cloud_adf_corpus.py`; an allowlist row needs an exact count) and the path to the parametrized `test_explicitly_excluded_paths_are_not_scanned` (fails before, passes after). (b) `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py::test_no_uncategorized_live_old_spelling` flagged the retired command names: add `".test_durations"` to its `_WHOLE_FILE_ALLOWLIST` (1 failed, 8 passed before; 9 passed after). (c) The review bot's `secret-detection` (gitleaks `private-key` rule, whole-file scan) flagged 3 locations, all parametrize ids of `test_create_rejects_all_private_key_headers` (a PEM header, a body of `x`, the END line): add a third `[[allowlists]]` entry to `.gitleaks.toml` scoped to that exact fake shape (header, body of exactly one `x`, END line), in the file's existing style of targeted fake-value allowlists, never a path exclusion. Before: 3 findings; after: 0; a real-shaped control key (200-character random body) is still flagged.

Known caveat (already on this ticket): the held-out merge epic traitorous-official-sunbittern (still open) renames or merges about 170 modules, which invalidates keys; its story awake-shoddy-gyrfalcon re-runs the same command at the end. Out of scope here.

## Scope
In scope: `.gitignore`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.test_durations` (new), `docs/local-dev-env.md`, `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` and its test `tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py` (one parameter case), `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py` (one allowlist entry) and `.gitleaks.toml` (one allowlist entry). Out of scope: any CI workflow that consumes the profile (`--splits`/`--group` is not wired into CI), `pyproject.toml`, the `Makefile`, and every other test module. No key-count ratchet is added: it would go stale with the merge epic.

## Red proof (before the change)
`git ls-files .test_durations` prints nothing; with the file present and the `exclude` unchanged, `pre-commit run check-added-large-files --files .test_durations` FAILS (over the 500 KB cap); after step 2 it passes.

## Testing
After the run: key count `python -c "import json;print(len(json.load(open('.test_durations'))))"`; collected count `pytest --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external" | tail -1`; nodes collected without a key and keys not collected are both counted and explained (target 0 each, since `--clean-durations` drops absent nodes); `pytest --splits 4 --group K --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external"` for K=1..4: the four counts sum to the collected count and the four estimated durations printed by pytest-split are each within 5% of a quarter of the total recorded time (groups are balanced by duration, so their test COUNTS differ, which a first draft of this plan got wrong); `pre-commit run --all-files` green; `python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check` green. Record the four counts, the file size and the host load on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.test_durations` is tracked (`git ls-files .test_durations` prints it), and the number of collected nodes with no key and of keys with no collected node are each recorded and explained (target 0), with the key count and collected count on this ticket.
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` accepts the file, and `pre-commit run check-added-large-files --files .test_durations` fails when the `exclude` change is reverted (red proof recorded).
- [ ] The `### Per-test durations (.test_durations)` section exists in `docs/local-dev-env.md` and `python scripts/check_docs_index.py --check` passes.
- [ ] For K=1..4, `pytest --splits 4 --group K --collect-only -q -m "not integration and not external"` collects counts that sum to the collected count, and the four estimated durations are each within 5% of a quarter of the total recorded time (counts and estimates recorded on this ticket).
- [ ] `python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` exits 0 with `.test_durations` tracked, and the new exclusion case in `tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py` fails without the `EXCLUDED_FILES` entry and passes with it (both runs recorded on this ticket).
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py` passes with `.test_durations` tracked, and fails without its allowlist entry (both runs recorded on this ticket).
- [ ] `gitleaks dir --config .gitleaks.toml .test_durations` reports 0 findings with the new `.gitleaks.toml` entry (3 `private-key` findings before), and a control file holding a PEM key with a 200-character random body is still reported (both outputs recorded on this ticket).
- [ ] `make verify` shows no failure outside the known pandoc set, and the Gerrit change is `Verified +1`.
